summary: Project RELIC is a semi platformer survival game where an astronaut with a mission to go to mars becomes stranded on the Moon after getting hit by a small solar flare. Being damaged he must used the hardware left on the Moon and Mars to patch up himself and his shuttle. This game addresses the challenge by making learning much more interactive and urgent. By having the need to survive and by using the parts left on the Moon and Mars, the user will have fun whilst learning about the different hardware.
details:
What It Does and How It Works

Project RELIC is a 2D survival semi-platformer that turns the history of NASA’s off-world hardware into an interactive rescue mission. Players step into the boots of an astronaut bound for Mars whose shuttle is damaged by a solar flare, leaving them stranded on the Moon with a cracked suit and a depleting oxygen supply.

To survive and repair their shuttle to reach and traverse Mars, players must navigate challenging terrain under strict oxygen limits to locate and scavenge components from real NASA spacecraft left on the lunar and Martian surfaces. The game features six iconic NASA artifacts across both worlds:

  • On the Moon: Surveyor 3 and the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
  • On Mars: Mars Pathfinder, the Sojourner rover, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and the Perseverance rover

Each time the player successfully reaches a piece of hardware and salvages parts to patch their suit or ship, they unlock accessible, story-driven logs detailing that artifact’s original mission, engineering design, and scientific discoveries.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Traditional space history archives can feel static or overwhelming, especially for younger learners. Project RELIC transforms passive reading into urgent, hands-on problem-solving. By tying survival mechanics directly to real spacecraft components, players naturally connect what each machine was built to do with how its engineering still matters today.

Designed for players of all ages—from school-age kids to adult space enthusiasts—the game sparks curiosity about planetary exploration and reframes "abandoned" equipment not as space junk, but as enduring milestones of human ingenuity that pave the way for future astronauts.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Game Engine & Programming: Built using the Godot Engine and coded in GDScript.
    • Font: "Quaver" by Nathan Scott (Caffinate)
    • Moon Surface: "Free Lunar Battle Pack" by MattWalkden
    • Earth and Space: "250+ Pixel art planets" by Helianthus Games
    • Astronaut: "Space Explorers" by PulsarCP
  • Target Hardware: Engineered and tested to run smoothly on standard and low-end computers without requiring dedicated graphics hardware.

How Our Project Is Creative

Rather than presenting spacecraft specs as a digital encyclopedia, Project RELIC weaves historical documentation into a high-stakes survival loop. Surviving a grueling platforming stretch while watching your oxygen meter drop makes discovering a dormant lander or rover feel like a genuine lifeline—mirroring the real-world Apollo 12 astronauts who visited Surveyor 3 on the Moon. Unlocking each artifact's story as a reward for scavenging gives silent, retired machines an active role in the player's survival.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Story-First Accessibility: We kept the platforming controls intuitive and easy to learn so mechanical difficulty enhances the tension without blocking players from progressing through the story.
  • Age-Inclusive Language: We deliberately avoided dense aerospace jargon in our in-game logs, translating complex mission histories into clear, engaging language that younger players can grasp while remaining faithful to NASA’s science.
  • Lightweight Performance: We optimized assets and scene complexity so Project RELIC remains lightweight and playable on low-end devices, ensuring broad access for students and casual players alike.
